clue.text: Square-rigger's fittings meet standards

parts.note: a square-rigged ship carries yards, the spars the square sails hang from
sailors call a ship's masts its sticks

explanation.surface: Gear aboard a square-rigged sailing ship meets the required standards.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both halves: the yards and the sticks (masts) of a square-rigger; 'meet' just joins them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Measuring rods used as a basis for comparison, so figuratively benchmarks or criteria.

clue.text: In boat, go off course on lake

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a ship that yaws swings off its heading
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone in a small boat drifts off course on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing craft with a small mizzen behind the rudder post, a type of vessel.

clue.text: When talking, it's good form

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for good sounds like another word with different spelling

parts.note: right means good or proper

explanation.surface: In conversation, it is considered good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony or set procedure is a prescribed form of observance.

clue.text: About noon, perverse juries order reply from plaintiff

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the letter for noon
perverse means contrary or twisted, so the letters of juries and order are jumbled

explanation.surface: Around midday a contrary jury orders a reply from the person who brought the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts the 'perverse' jumble of the two clue words around noon's letter; 'order' looks like a verb for the jury but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In old common-law pleading, the plaintiff's answer to the defendant's rejoinder was called this.

clue.text: Take part of pride — a lioness, for example

indicators.note: the answer is a portion of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Among a pride of lions, a lioness is held up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'prIDE A Lioness'; 'pride' looks like the lions' group but only lends its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect model to aspire to, a paragon or exemplar.

clue.text: Perform in front of an audience, and run home

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece stands before, above, the second

parts.note: to keep a promise or a rule is to perform or observe it
a theatre's house is its audience

explanation.surface: An actor plays to a crowd, then dashes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perform' and 'audience' suggest the stage, but 'keep' is perform as in fulfil, and 'house' is the theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a household's affairs, as a housekeeper does.

clue.text: Pay wife out for a long time

indicators.note: out means the letter for wife is removed from the word for pay

parts.note: wages are pay

explanation.surface: Paying out the wife's allowance takes forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic: it took ages means it lasted a very long while.

clue.text: One delivering, sustaining a note — he's responsible for the pitch

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up, sustains, the one above it

parts.note: G is a musical note
a roundsman delivers milk or bread on a round

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler delivering the ball, or a singer holding a note, near a pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One delivering' and 'pitch' suggest a bowler, or a singer holding a note; 'sustaining' puts ROUNDSMAN beneath G.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends a sports ground, preparing the playing surface.

clue.text: Governor in Holland has toddler in odd get-up

indicators.note: an odd get-up is a strange arrangement of clothing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dutch official's toddler is dressed in a strange outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical title of the chief magistrate of the Dutch Republic or of a province, a Dutch viceroy.

clue.text: Matter we're resolving — a way to determine liquid intake

definitions.text: a way to determine liquid intake

indicators.note: resolving means breaking up and reforming, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A problem we are settling turns out to be about measuring drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A device recording the volume of supply a household takes in from the mains.

clue.text: First in one test, am I?

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are top in one examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'in one test am' spell the name of the Greek letter written as I, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet corresponds to the Roman letter written as a single stroke.

clue.text: What people like best is a new present to use

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: What people prefer is a fresh gift ready to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PRESENT TO USE; 'is a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for something suiting a person's tastes or abilities exactly.

clue.text: Want bird stuffed with fish, a bit of thyme with it

indicators.note: a bird stuffed is filled, so the other pieces go inside its word

parts.note: a finch is a small bird
an eel is a fish

indicators.note: a bit of means just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: hep is old slang for fashionable or with it

explanation.surface: A recipe: a small bird filled with fish and a sprig of thyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb of desire but is the definition; 'with it' is old slang, and 'a bit of' takes only thyme's first letter, all 'stuffed' into the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Want here is the noun-turned-verb of poverty: to suffer hardship from lack of money is to be in want.

clue.text: Pope keeps Templar safe

parts.note: Simon Templar is the fictional hero known as the Saint
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: The Pope keeps a Knight Templar safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Templar' suggests the medieval knights, but it is Simon Templar, the Saint of Leslie Charteris's novels; 'keeps' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle known by both names is counted as the first bishop of Rome, the first pontiff.

clue.text: In escalating orbits, I had to follow a star like the earth

indicators.note: in means the following pieces sit inside the reversed word
escalating means going up, which in a down clue reads a word upwards, backwards

parts.note: laps are circuits or orbits

indicators.note: to follow puts the short piece after the one it follows

parts.note: a hero is a star, a celebrated person
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: An astronomer explains that a planet circled ever higher after a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escalating' turns the word for orbits upwards to SPAL, and 'In' puts the star and I'd inside it, the contraction coming second because of 'to follow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is roughly ball-shaped, slightly flattened at the poles, a spheroid.

clue.text: I am ready to act; you, I hear, are offhand

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
prompt means quick and ready to act

indicators.note: I hear means the word you is spoken and written as the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone says they are ready, while the other person sounds casual.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without preparation, improvised on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: A dainty little boat?

parts.note: petit is French for little
a four is a rowing boat for four oarsmen

explanation.surface: A small, delicate boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dainty' looks like an adjective for the boat, but it is a noun, a delicacy; the question mark flags the rowing sense of four.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fancy cake or biscuit served after a meal is a delicacy.

clue.text: Hooter's left behind by spacemen

indicators.note: behind means the letter comes after the other piece

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency

explanation.surface: Someone's nose has been left behind by astronauts.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is slang for nose, so 'Hooter's' is the adjective, of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the nose, as a nasal voice or nasal spray.

clue.text: The main defect of a canoe

indicators.note: a defect is a fault, so the letters of canoe come out wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: The chief flaw of a canoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' looks like 'the chief', but it is the old poetic word for the sea; 'defect of' rearranges CANOE.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary name for the open sea.

clue.text: Plant's almost leafless, so reptile can be seen

parts.note: a tree is a plant, and 's supplies an S

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a leafless plant is naked, bare

explanation.surface: A plant has nearly lost its leaves, so a snake can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboreal serpent is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: The status of Bechuanaland in the Commonwealth

definitions.text: The status of Bechuanaland in the Commonwealth

parts.words: The status of Bechuanaland in the Commonwealth
parts.note: Bechuanaland, now Botswana, was a British-administered territory rather than a colony until 1966

explanation.definitionFit: Bechuanaland was formally a British dependent territory of this kind, under Crown protection.

clue.text: Regretting bankruptcy? Good!

parts.note: financial ruin is bankruptcy

explanation.surface: Someone regrets going bust, and another person is glad.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, so this participle means regretting.

clue.text: Blue clue may be

definitions.meaning: feeling blue means sad or low
a crossword clue is either across or in the other direction

explanation.definitionFit: Low in spirits; and the second direction of crossword clues besides across.

clue.text: Paid the fare

definitions.meaning: fare is food, and to provide it is to nourish

explanation.definitionFit: Paid a fee to, as in fee'd; and gave food, as in provided fare for.

clue.text: Fuss caused by item about duke

indicators.note: about means the word for item goes round the letter for duke

parts.note: item is an old word meaning also or likewise

explanation.surface: A fuss is made over something concerning a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item' looks like a noun, but here it is the old adverb meaning also, giving TOO; 'caused by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or bother is a fuss.

clue.text: See American town in a caravan

parts.note: Mobile is a city in Alabama
home means in, at home

explanation.surface: A visitor is invited to see an American town from inside a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it gives HOME, as in 'stay in'; 'See' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a towed or wheeled dwelling, a house on the move.

clue.text: Register thunder

definitions.meaning: a register is an official list of names

explanation.definitionFit: An official list of names; and a prolonged rumble, as of drums or thunder.

clue.text: Windy fellow put straight

parts.note: righted or rightened means set straight

explanation.surface: A breezy man straightened things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy' suggests weather, but it is old slang for scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy is British slang for nervous or afraid.
